newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Holding wraps up Elektrowatt withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: CS Holding wraps up Elektrowatt withdrawal.

text.p: Swiss financial group CS Holding on Monday wrapped up its long-intended withdrawal from industrial holdings by selling a large part of Elektrowatt AG to German electronics giant Siemens AG.
The sale to Siemens of Elektrowatt's industrial activities follows last week's deal in which CS Holding agreed to sell the energy activities of Elektrowatt to a Swiss-German consortium.

"In concentrating on our core business we have sought a new shareholder structure for Elektrowatt. We are delighted that viable and promising solutions have been found for both the energy and industry segments," CS Holding's chairman Rainer Gut said in a statement.

CS Holding will sell most of its 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt, one of the world's leading building control and security system companies, for more than two billion Swiss francs, resulting in a book profit of around one billion.

This profit will directly offset charges of a similar amount that CS Holding took in July to cover the costs of a major restructuring of the group, including changing the name to Credit Suisse Group and cutting some 5,000 jobs worldwide.
"The one billion net profit from the sale will be offset against restructuring charges," a CS Holding spokesman said.

The gain from the sale will not change CS Holding's forecast for this year, which calls for a net loss of 2.1 billion francs due to charges of 3.9 billion from provisions in connection with a change in the method for calculating credit risks.
Excluding these charges, CS Holding's net profit in 1996 would have risen some 17 percent to 1.8 billion francs.
CS Holding's divestment of its stake in Elektrowatt has been a lengthy process that required many individual steps.

The process began in November when Elektrowatt announced it would spin-off its power and electricity activities into a separate company, Watt AG. CS Holding would retain a 44.9 percent stake in Watt and in the remaining Elektrowatt.
Elektrowatt's shareholders are scheduled to vote on the split of the company in February.

Last week CS Holding then sold off around 30 percent of its shares in Watt for around one billion francs to a consortium comprising German energy companies Bayernwerk, Badenwerk and Energieversorgung Schwaben (EVS) and Swiss utility Nordostschweizerische Kraftwerke (NOK).
The sale to Siemens of its 44.9 percent stake in the industrial activities of Elektrowatt completes the process.
Following the expected spin-off of Watt in February, Siemens will take over CS Holding's shares in Elektrowatt for 285 francs a share, or around 1.1 billion francs.
Siemens will then make a public offer to other Elektrowatt shareholders at the same price.
Siemens intends to make Landis & Staefa, respectively Cerberus and Landis & Gyr Utilities, the focal point of its worldwide activites in building control and security systems.
